sources.entry: Loupe - Accessibility inspector that generates AI-agent-ready output. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/britchie4/Loupe) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Loupe is a macOS accessibility inspector that lets you hover over or click UI elements in any Mac app and produces structured, agent-readable output to paste into AI coding assistants.
summary.what_it_does: Loupe shows accessibility information for any UI element in any Mac app as you hover over it in real time. You can click an element and write a plain-English description of the change you want. It then copies structured output containing element roles, hierarchy paths, and search patterns, which you paste into an AI assistant such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex so the assistant can target the exact element without screenshots. The README says version 1.2.1 and later update themselves, with an option to check for updates automatically, and older versions are updated by manually replacing the app.
use_cases: inspect accessibility info of a Mac app element
give an AI coding assistant precise UI targets
speed up Mac app development with Claude Code
annotate UI changes for an AI agent
how_to_run: Download Loupe (.dmg) from the latest release
Grant Accessibility permission when prompted on first launch
notable: Hover-to-inspect accessibility info for any element in any Mac app
Annotate an element and generate copy-ready output for AI agents
Output includes element roles, hierarchy paths, and search patterns
Inspired by agentation.dev, the web equivalent
caveats: Needs Accessibility permission granted on first launch
Versions before 1.2.1 must be updated manually
